'''Chen Tiemei''' ({{lang-zh|s=陈铁梅}}; 30 June 1935 – 25 October 2018) was a Chinese physicist and archaeologist, considered a pioneer in scientific archaeology and a founder of quantitative archaeology in China. He was a professor and Director of the Scientific Archaeology Laboratory at [[Peking University]].

== Life and career ==
Chen was born on 30 June 1935 in [[Shanghai]], Republic of China. After graduating from [[Shanghai High School]] in 1952, he tested into the Department of Physics of [[Peking University]]. In August 1954, he was sent by the Chinese government to study physics at [[Leningrad University]] in the Soviet Union.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://archaeology.pku.edu.cn/Faculty/e/2018/11/2/154112340261.shtml|title=Chen Tiemei|last=|first=|date=|website=Peking University|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190515040350/http://archaeology.pku.edu.cn/Faculty/e/2018/11/2/154112340261.shtml|archive-date=2019-05-15|access-date=2019-05-15|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_2568144|title=北京大学考古文博学院教授、著名科技考古学家陈铁梅逝世|last=|first=|date=2018-10-26|website=The Paper|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-05-15}}</ref>

Upon graduation in 1959, Chen returned to China to teach at the [[Dalian Institute of Technology]]. In 1961, he became a faculty member of the Department of Technical Physics at Peking University. In 1973, he was transferred to the Department of Archaeology and served as Director of the Scientific Archaeology Laboratory. He became a full professor of archaeology in 1989 and a doctoral advisor in 1994.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> He was proficient in English and Russian, and taught himself German and Japanese. He was a corresponding member of the [[German Archaeological Institute]].<ref name=":0" />

Chen died on 25 October 2018 in Beijing, at the age of 83.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bjnews.com.cn/news/2018/10/26/514561.html|title=著名科技考古学家陈铁梅逝世 曾提出我国第一个旧石器考古年表|last=|first=|date=2018-10-26|website=The Beijing News|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-05-15}}</ref>

== Contributions ==
A pioneer in scientific archaeology, Chen established China's first [[radiocarbon dating]] laboratory using [[liquid scintillation counting]] at Peking University.<ref name="Wang2014">{{cite book|editor=Wang Wei 王巍|script-title=zh:中国考古学大辞典|trans-title=Great Dictionary of Chinese Archaeology|year=2014|publisher=Shanghai Cishu Chubanshe|isbn=978-7-5326-4027-0|oclc=889734502|language=zh|pages=96–97}}</ref> He was instrumental in establishing laboratories and training personnel for carbon-14 dating in China.<ref name=":0" /> He dated more than 20 [[palaeolithic]] and [[paleoanthropological]] sites, and proposed the first chronology for [[Palaeolithic China]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name="Wang2014" /> From the early 1990s, Chen pioneered and developed scientific methods to determine the geographical origins of ancient ceramics and porcelain.<ref name=":0" />

Chen published more than 30 papers in influential journals including ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' and ''[[Acta Archaeologica Sinica]]''.<ref name=":0" /> He served as an editor of domestic and international journals including ''[[Quaternary Science Reviews]]'' and ''[[Quaternary Geochronology]]''.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Wang2014" />

After retiring from Peking University, Chen dedicated himself to writing. He published the monographs ''Quantitative Archaeology'' (定量考古学) in 2005, ''Scientific Archaeology'' (科技考古学) in 2008, and ''Concise Statistics for Archaeology'' (简明考古统计学) in 2013.<ref name=":0" />
